description: Thrives in high-humidity coastal areas with laterite soil and heavy monsoon rains.
A highly salt-tolerant coastal crop that thrives in sandy laterite soils near the seaboard. Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu coasts are ideal.
A tropical crop that grows well across Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and eastern coastal plains. Requires warm temperatures and consistent moisture.
The 'King of Spices' — grows as a vine on trees in the humid Western Ghats foothills of Kerala and Karnataka. Requires high humidity and well-drained soil.
Grows in high-altitude forests of the Western Ghats (Idukki, Wayanad, Kodagu). Requires cool, shaded conditions and heavy rainfall.
A high-value spice crop grown in Kerala, NE India, and coastal Andhra. Prefers well-drained loamy soils with shade.
A spice crop widely grown in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, and Odisha. Needs warm temperatures and well-distributed rainfall.
Requires well-drained loamy or red soil, hilly elevation, and moderate, cool temperatures.
A highly water-intensive crop perfect for heavy monsoon regions with clayey or alluvial soils. Coastal varieties like Jyothi (Kerala) and Samba (TN) thrive near the coast.
A rabi (winter) crop that requires cool temperatures and moderate water.
Highly adaptable crop that grows well in moderately warm and semi-dry regions.
Perfect for the Deccan plateau; requires deep black soil and dry harvest periods.
A cash crop needing long, hot summers and consistent irrigation year-round.
Grows excellently in coastal laterite soils with minimal maintenance. Widely cultivated in Goa, Kerala, and Maharashtra coast.
A major oilseed crop in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka. Requires well-drained sandy-loam soil.
A kharif oilseed crop widely grown in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan.
A rabi (winter) oilseed crop grown in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, and West Bengal. Tolerates cold and semi-arid conditions.
A versatile oilseed crop adaptable to many soils. Grows well in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
Extremely drought-resistant crop suitable for dry regions with poor soil fertility.
The most drought-tolerant cereal. Ideal for arid Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Haryana. Can withstand extreme heat and minimal rainfall.
A major fibre crop grown in West Bengal, Assam, Bihar, and Odisha's alluvial plains. Thrives in hot, humid, and waterlogged conditions.
A starch-rich tuber crop widely grown in Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Tolerates poor, sandy, and laterite soils common along the coast.
A high-value cash crop grown in Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, and Odisha. Requires humid, warm conditions and well-drained soils.
Coastal paddy varieties (Jyothi, Samba Masuri, BPT-5204) are salt-tolerant and grow in coastal deltaic regions of Andhra, Kerala, Odisha, and West Bengal.
India's most popular fruit. Grows across Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, and Gujarat. Tolerates dry spells during flowering.
A plantation crop cultivated in Kerala's midland laterite slopes. Requires consistently high rainfall and warm temperatures year-round.
Grown in the high-altitude zones of Assam, West Bengal (Darjeeling), and Nilgiris. Requires cool, misty conditions and well-drained, acidic soil.
